source.title: A shared neural ensemble links distinct contextual memories encoded close in time

confidence_rationale: Nature paper with in-vivo miniscope imaging of CA1 ensembles plus causal excitability manipulation, directly demonstrating that TEMPORAL DISTANCE between two encoding episodes determines hippocampal ensemble overlap (linking within a day vs separation across a week). This is the most direct empirical grounding for temporal distance as a first-class gating variable. Held below 0.8 because it isolates the excitability/temporal-window mechanism (a bottom-up allocation rule) rather than the top-down PFC policy, and the mapping to a REE temporal-gap weight is by analogy.
failure_signatures: The temporal-window linking here is driven by intrinsic neuronal excitability dynamics, NOT by a top-down control decision -- so this paper supports temporal distance as a VARIABLE but is silent on whether a control plane should set its weight; over-reading it as evidence for the POLICY would be a category error.

Increased excitability and short-window linking are absent in aged animals, indicating the temporal-distance effect is itself substrate-conditional and not a fixed law -- a REE temporal_gap term would inherit that state-dependence.
The effect is a memory-linking (co-recall) bias, not a demonstration of harmful false association; mapping it to a reality-coherence cost requires the separate over-generalization literature.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Two distinct contexts encoded within a day share a higher-overlap CA1 ensemble (and become behaviourally linked: recall of one biases recall of the other) than contexts encoded a week apart; the linking is mediated by a learning-triggered transient increase in neuronal excitability that biases allocation of the second memory toward the first memory's ensemble.
mapping.ree_translation: Direct empirical support for the intake's `temporal_distance` (days-vs-hours) gating variable: the time gap between two encoding episodes is a real, measurable determinant of whether traces are allocated to overlapping or separate representations. In REE terms this grounds the `temporal_gap_weight(estimate_temporal_distance(...))` term in the allocate_memory_trace sketch -- short gap -> integration pressure, long gap -> separation -- and identifies an excitability/allocation-bias mechanism (cf. MECH-261 awake-reactivation bias) as the substrate the temporal term would actuate.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is a BOTTOM-UP allocation rule (intrinsic excitability time-window), complementary to but distinct from the de Sousa TOP-DOWN PFC policy. It justifies temporal distance as an input variable; it does not show a control plane setting the temporal weight. The REE translation to a tunable temporal_gap_weight is an architectural analogy, and the effect's absence in aged animals means the weight is state-conditional, not constant.
mapping.source_context: Mouse; open-field / fear-context memory-linking paradigm with encoding episodes 5 h to 7 days apart; head-mounted miniature-microscope CA1 calcium imaging + CREB/excitability manipulation.

confidence_components.notes: High source quality (Nature, longitudinal single-cell ensemble imaging + causal excitability manipulation, foundational and well-cited). Mapping fidelity high for the temporal-distance variable specifically -- this is close to a 1:1 grounding of the temporal_gap term. Transfer risk moderate (rodent ensemble allocation -> REE trace allocation; state-conditional effect).
